value.account: Two defects stacked. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted rejected any relpath output before checking for the compiler-emitted exhausted-placeholder ref; at 2.29+ the compiler emits that ref for the inactive path field. I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath rejection. It is still an exact match against the refs the lowering captured and is only enabled during lowering, so authored relpath overrides are still rejected (existing test_loader_validation case still passes). (2) Once it compiled, the run failed at exhaustion: orchestrator/workflow/loops.py stored the on_exhausted {'ref':...} overrides verbatim in the loop frame, and at 2.29+ the result join reads result__rounds from the frame (2.28 routed it to state__round), so it saw a dict and failed 'invalid_integer'. repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts now resolves such refs (own-loop refs from the exhaustion snapshot, others from persisted step artifacts), gated on workflow version >= 2.29 so <=2.28 is untouched; unresolved refs raise. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths_e2e.py runs a union-result loop at 2.28..2.32 through the real executor: exhaustion (same outputs as 2.28), done path, and a missing report path from the provider still fails. Ran that module plus test_workflow_loops_exhaustion_state, test_loader_validation, test_workflow_lisp_loop_recur: 288 passed. Considered: relaxing the validator for all relpath overrides (weakens validation, rejected); making the 2.29 compiler route return__rounds to state__round like 2.28 (more invasive in lowering). Not covered: the repro in bugs/ was only dry-run compiled, not run with real providers; the other test modules (full suite) were not run; resumed runs that exhaust were not specifically tested; refs inside nested call/loop scopes beyond root.steps names were not exercised.
value.summary: Loop results with a path field in a non-exhausted variant now compile and run at 2.29-2.32 identically to 2.28, via two small fixes (validator ordering, runtime resolution of exhaustion refs).

value.account: Two defects. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py `_validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted`: the 'may only override scalar' relpath rejection ran before the check for compiler-generated on_exhausted refs, so the compiler's own placeholder ref for an inactive-variant relpath field (emitted from 2.29 by rich loop values) was rejected. I moved the generated-ref check first; it only matches the exact ref the compiler recorded, and only when the allow flag (compiler path) is set, so authored YAML relpath overrides are still rejected (tests/test_loader_validation.py case still passes). (2) Fixing only that exposed a runtime failure on exhaustion: orchestrator/workflow/loops.py `repeat_until_exhaustion_artifacts` stored on_exhausted `{ref: ...}` overrides unresolved, and from 2.29 the result match join reads those loop outputs (at 2.28 it read state__round and the frame's placeholder directly), so validation saw a dict instead of a relpath/int. It now resolves such refs at exhaustion (self refs from the frame artifacts, other refs via the executor's ref resolver; unresolvable refs are left as before), gated on workflow version >= 2.29 so 2.28 and earlier are untouched. Regression tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_union_paths.py runs the program end to end at 2.28-2.32 via run_workflow with stubbed providers: exhaustion gives UNRESOLVED/rounds=2, approval gives READY with the report, and a provider path '../escape.md' still fails the run. Verified targeted modules (loop/exhaustion/rich-loop/lowering/wcc/loader-validation etc.) pass; test_workflow_lisp_key_migrations.py has 6 failures (resume_state_path_unsafe) that are identical on the unmodified tree. Alternatives considered: emitting a literal placeholder from the compiler (would need loosening the relpath validator for literals, a wider weakening) and gating the runtime join to skip inactive variants (no variant metadata is present on these join outputs). Not covered: nested/non-root scopes where the root.steps ref cannot be resolved fall back to the old raw-ref behaviour; I did not run the full suite or resume/replay of an exhausted run; docs not updated.
value.summary: At targets 2.29-2.32 the loop's exhaustion placeholder ref for a relpath field is now accepted by validation and resolved at runtime, so the reported program compiles and runs identically to 2.28.

value.account: Root cause had two layers. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py _validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted rejected any override on a relpath output before checking whether it was the compiler-generated loop-frame ref (the placeholder ref that 2.29+ lowering emits for the inactive-variant path field). I moved the generated-ref check ahead of the relpath rejection; that check is only enabled for Workflow Lisp lowering and matches the exact expected ref, so authored YAML overrides on path outputs are still rejected (existing test_loader_validation case still passes). (2) Once compiled, the 2.29+ exhaustion run failed at runtime: the loop frame stores on_exhausted overrides as {ref: ...} dicts and the structured match join (executor._resolve_structured_output_artifacts) validated the dict itself, giving invalid_relpath/invalid_integer. This failure also affected plain scalar results (result__rounds ref to the loop's own state) on baseline 2.32, even with no path fields. Fix: in that function, a raw value that is exactly {ref: str} for an output whose declared type is string/integer/float/bool/enum/relpath is chased through _resolve_ref_value before validation (such types can never legitimately be a mapping; records/maps/lists are untouched; resolved values are still contract-validated, so malformed provider output still fails). 2.28 and earlier never produce ref values at the join, so unchanged. Alternatives: (a) compiler omits the override for path fields as 2.28 does - discarded as it would not fix the scalar self-ref failure and would diverge from rich-loop lowering; (b) resolve refs when building exhausted frame artifacts in workflow/loops.py - I tried it for path outputs; it fixed paths but not the scalar self-ref (not yet in state) and would change persisted 2.28 loop artifacts, so reverted. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_paths.py (compile at 2.28-2.32, exhaustion and approval runs at 2.28 and 2.32 through the public runner with stubbed providers, malformed provider path still fails). Ran that plus test_loader_validation, rich_loop_values_e2e, scoped_union_guards, loops_exhaustion_state, loop_recur: 314 passed. Not covered: active-variant path field projected from loop state on exhaustion at 2.29+ (not tested end to end), resume across exhaustion, nested loops, other ref-consuming read paths besides the structured join; full suite not run.
value.summary: At targets 2.29-2.32 loop/recur union results with path fields in an inactive variant now compile (validator accepts compiler-generated ref overrides on path outputs) and run to exhaustion identically to 2.28 (structured join chases loop-frame ref overrides for scalar/path outputs).

value.account: Two root causes, both only hit at target >=2.29. (1) orchestrator/workflow/validation.py `_validate_repeat_until_on_exhausted`: the 'may only override scalar' check ran before the check for the exact compiler-emitted loop-frame ref, so the generated placeholder ref that 2.29+ lowering emits for a path field of an inactive variant (result__report -> <loop>__exhausted_placeholders) was rejected. I moved the generated-ref check first; it is still gated on the lowering-only option and an exact ref match, so authored refs and literals on relpath outputs are still rejected (new loader test added). (2) After compile, exhaustion failed at runtime: orchestrator/workflow/executor.py `_resolve_structured_output_artifacts` validated the loop's persisted on_exhausted ref payload ({"ref": ...}) directly against the relpath/integer contract, so the match join failed with invalid_relpath/invalid_integer (this also affected scalar refs such as state.round in 2.29+ union results with no path field at all). It now resolves such a ref payload through the existing _resolve_ref_value before validating; resolved values still go through validate_contract_value, so malformed values still fail. Persisted loop artifacts are unchanged. Tests: tests/test_workflow_lisp_loop_result_inactive_path_variants.py runs the program end to end (fake providers) for exhaustion, approve and escalate at 2.29-2.32 and asserts workflow outputs equal 2.28's, plus a malformed-report run that still fails; tests/test_loader_validation.py gains an authored-ref rejection test. Targeted modules (loop_recur, rich_loop_values_e2e, loops_exhaustion_state, loader_validation, lowering, loop_state, nested_loop, executor_characterization, etc.) pass: 567 + new. Alternatives discarded: resolving all on_exhausted refs at loop commit time in loops.py (worked, but changed persisted artifacts and broke test_loop_recur_on_exhausted_scalar_frame_carriage which asserts the persisted ref); changing the lowering to skip the placeholder ref at 2.29+ (would diverge from the deliberate rich-loop-values design and 2.28 literal placeholder semantics). Not covered: full test suite (not run per instructions); the resume path for a run interrupted between exhaustion and the join was not separately exercised; the resolver follows any {"ref"}-only dict value reaching a structured output join, not only exhaustion overrides.
value.summary: Accepted the compiler-generated exhaustion ref on path outputs in validation and resolved exhaustion ref payloads at structured-output joins, so 2.29-2.32 loop results with inactive-variant path fields compile and run like 2.28.
